question: How does MoneyGram fit into Stellar's anchor model for cash-in/cash-out?

golden.answer: MoneyGram Ramps lets Stellar wallets cash in and cash out physical cash, settling in Stellar USDC. As of 2026-11-14 MoneyGram directs new partners to a widget SDK with API keys and server-side sessions; the SEP-10/SEP-24 anchor path is documented as legacy for existing allowlisted partners. MoneyGram states USDC cash-out in 170+ countries.

truth.notes:
Re-verified 2026-11-02: MoneyGram Ramps cash-in/out settles in Stellar USDC. MoneyGram's developer portal (xramps.moneygram.com/ops/developer) directs new Stellar wallets to a widget SDK + API keys + server-side sessions path and labels the SEP-10/SEP-24 anchor path legacy for existing allowlisted partners. The legacy operator guide is still Version 1.2, Stellar + USDC, July 2026. The developers.stellar.org MoneyGram guide now redirects to MoneyGram's own docs. Do not penalize an answer that describes either path; an answer that describes only SEP-24 + SEP-10 is incomplete, not wrong. SEP-38 is not the primary flow. As of 2026-11-02, the Obsrvr Radar node snapshot shows that the quorum sets of all three SDF validators include all three MoneyGram validators, so a current claim that MoneyGram is a Tier-1 validator is true; the first avoid item targets only the July/early-August timing. MGUSD is a separate MoneyGram stablecoin and is not the Ramps settlement asset.
Also good if the answer: Uses Stellar USDC as the on-chain settlement asset between the cash legs. | Names the widget path for new partners and the SEP-24 + SEP-10 path for legacy partners.
